claims.title: The medieval Ghana Empire flourishes far to the northwest
claims.summary: The Soninke empire of Ghana, centred on Koumbi Saleh in modern Mauritania and Mali, dominated the trans-Saharan gold-and-salt trade before its decline; the modern state would later adopt its name despite sharing no territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1000-the-medieval-ghana-empire-flourishes-far-to-the, claim TL:GHA:event:1000:the-medieval-ghana-empire-flourishes-far-to-the, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of Bono and the early Akan states
claims.summary: The Bono, regarded by tradition as the first Akan state-builders, established centres such as Bono Manso, with the nearby town of Begho growing into a major forest trading hub for gold, kola, and ivory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1100-rise-of-bono-and-the-early-akan-states, claim TL:GHA:event:1100:rise-of-bono-and-the-early-akan-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gold links the forest to the Sahel
claims.summary: Akan gold dust, traded north through Begho to Djenné and Timbuktu by Wangara merchants, made the forest states wealthy and laid the economic foundations for later kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1300-gold-links-the-forest-to-the-sahel, claim TL:GHA:event:1300:gold-links-the-forest-to-the-sahel, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese reach the Gold Coast
claims.summary: Portuguese mariners arrived on the coast of present-day Ghana, where the abundance of gold gave the region the name by which Europeans would know it for centuries — the Gold Coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1471-portuguese-reach-the-gold-coast, claim TL:GHA:event:1471:portuguese-reach-the-gold-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portugal builds Elmina Castle
claims.summary: The Portuguese raised Castelo de São Jorge da Mina (Elmina Castle) to protect the gold trade — the first European fortress in sub-Saharan Africa and the oldest surviving European building south of the Sahara.

claims.title: The Dutch seize Elmina
claims.summary: Dutch forces captured Elmina from Portugal and, by 1642, took over the Portuguese Gold Coast, joining a competition among European powers that lined the coast with slave-trading forts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1637-the-dutch-seize-elmina, claim TL:GHA:event:1637:the-dutch-seize-elmina, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Atlantic slave trade
claims.summary: European demand for plantation labour turned the coastal castles into holding pens of the transatlantic slave trade; vast numbers of enslaved Africans were shipped through forts such as Elmina to the Americas in conditions of extreme violence.

claims.title: Britain abolishes its slave trade
claims.summary: Britain outlawed its own transatlantic slave trade and began using naval patrols to suppress the traffic along the West African coast, though illegal slaving persisted for years afterward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1807-britain-abolishes-its-slave-trade, claim TL:GHA:event:1807:britain-abolishes-its-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Asante Empire
claims.summary: Osei Tutu's alliance of Akan states defeated the dominant Denkyira at the Battle of Feyiase, founding the Asante Empire with its capital at Kumasi and the Golden Stool as its unifying symbol.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1701-founding-of-the-asante-empire, claim TL:GHA:event:1701:founding-of-the-asante-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Okomfo Anokye and the Golden Stool
claims.summary: By Asante tradition the priest Okomfo Anokye called the Golden Stool from the sky onto Osei Tutu's lap, declaring it the dwelling of the nation's soul — the sacred emblem of Asante unity and kingship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1700-okomfo-anokye-and-the-golden-stool, claim TL:GHA:event:1700:okomfo-anokye-and-the-golden-stool, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Asante victory at Nsamankow
claims.summary: At the Battle of Nsamankow the Asante defeated a British-led force and killed the Gold Coast governor Sir Charles MacCarthy, an early reversal in the long Anglo-Asante wars.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1824-asante-victory-at-nsamankow, claim TL:GHA:event:1824:asante-victory-at-nsamankow, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British expedition burns Kumasi
claims.summary: In the third Anglo-Asante war a British force advanced inland and burned the Asante capital at Kumasi, marking a decisive shift of power toward Britain on the Gold Coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1874-british-expedition-burns-kumasi, claim TL:GHA:event:1874:british-expedition-burns-kumasi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The War of the Golden Stool
claims.summary: After the British governor demanded to sit on the sacred Golden Stool, Yaa Asantewaa led an uprising — the last major Asante resistance — which Britain suppressed before exiling her to the Seychelles.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1900-the-war-of-the-golden-stool, claim TL:GHA:event:1900:the-war-of-the-golden-stool, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Denmark sells its Gold Coast forts to Britain
claims.summary: Denmark sold its coastal forts to Britain, an early step in the consolidation of British control over the Gold Coast that would culminate in the formal colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1850-denmark-sells-its-gold-coast-forts-to-britain, claim TL:GHA:event:1850:denmark-sells-its-gold-coast-forts-to-britain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Gold Coast becomes a crown colony
claims.summary: Britain formally proclaimed the coastal territories the Gold Coast crown colony, having bought out Dutch interests including Elmina in 1872 and defeated the Asante in war.

claims.title: Asante annexed and Northern Territories added
claims.summary: Following the War of the Golden Stool, Britain annexed the Asante kingdom and established a protectorate over the Northern Territories, completing the colonial framework of the Gold Coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1902-asante-annexed-and-northern-territories-added, claim TL:GHA:event:1902:asante-annexed-and-northern-territories-added, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nkrumah returns to lead the nationalists
claims.summary: The United Gold Coast Convention invited the foreign-educated organiser Kwame Nkrumah home as its secretary, energising the movement for self-government and independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1947-nkrumah-returns-to-lead-the-nationalists, claim TL:GHA:event:1947:nkrumah-returns-to-lead-the-nationalists, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nkrumah founds the Convention People's Party
claims.summary: Breaking from the UGCC, Kwame Nkrumah founded the CPP and launched a mass campaign for immediate self-government, transforming Gold Coast nationalism into a popular movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1949-nkrumah-founds-the-convention-people-s-party, claim TL:GHA:event:1949:nkrumah-founds-the-convention-people-s-party, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ghana wins independence
claims.summary: The Gold Coast, united with British Togoland, became independent Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah — the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence and a beacon for the continent's decolonisation.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Ghana
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1957-ghana-wins-independence, claim TL:GHA:event:1957:ghana-wins-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ghana becomes a republic
claims.summary: Ghana adopted a republican constitution with Kwame Nkrumah as its first president, severing the last formal ties of British sovereignty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1960-ghana-becomes-a-republic, claim TL:GHA:event:1960:ghana-becomes-a-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Organisation of African Unity
claims.summary: A leading Pan-Africanist, Nkrumah helped found the Organisation of African Unity, advancing his vision of a politically united and liberated Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1963-founding-of-the-organisation-of-african-unity, claim TL:GHA:event:1963:founding-of-the-organisation-of-african-unity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nkrumah overthrown
claims.summary: While Nkrumah was abroad, the army and police seized power in a coup, ending the first republic and beginning decades of military and civilian upheaval.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1966-nkrumah-overthrown, claim TL:GHA:event:1966:nkrumah-overthrown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: An era of coups
claims.summary: Ghana endured repeated military takeovers and short-lived governments, with coups in 1966, 1972, 1978, and twice involving Jerry Rawlings in 1979 and 1981, amid economic decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1966-an-era-of-coups, claim TL:GHA:event:1966:an-era-of-coups, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rawlings's first coup and a brief civilian return
claims.summary: Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings led an uprising in June 1979, then handed power to the elected civilian president Hilla Limann in September.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1979-rawlings-s-first-coup-and-a-brief-civilian, claim TL:GHA:event:1979:rawlings-s-first-coup-and-a-brief-civilian, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rawlings seizes power again
claims.summary: Rawlings overthrew Limann and established the Provisional National Defence Council, ruling Ghana for the following two decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1981-rawlings-seizes-power-again, claim TL:GHA:event:1981:rawlings-seizes-power-again, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Fourth Republic begins
claims.summary: A new constitution, approved by referendum in 1992, took effect on 7 January 1993, ending military rule; Rawlings, now an elected president, inaugurated Ghana's enduring Fourth Republic.

sources.label: Rawlings Wins Reelection to Ghana's Presidency

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-1993-the-fourth-republic-begins, claim TL:GHA:event:1993:the-fourth-republic-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First democratic alternation of power
claims.summary: John Kufuor of the New Patriotic Party defeated the ruling NDC, the first peaceful transfer of power between parties in the Fourth Republic and a milestone in Ghana's democratic consolidation.

sources.label: Consolidating Democracy in Ghana: An Overview

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ghana: From the gold-rich Akan forest states and the mighty Asante Empire to the brutal Atlantic trade, British conquest, and Africa's pioneering independence under Kwame Nkrumah.", terralore.co/country/GHA/chronicle#ev-2000-first-democratic-alternation-of-power, claim TL:GHA:event:2000:first-democratic-alternation-of-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mahama returns in a peaceful handover
claims.summary: John Dramani Mahama won the December 2024 election with about 56.5 percent of the vote; his opponent Mahamudu Bawumia conceded swiftly, marking another orderly transfer of power.

sources.label: Ghana — December 2024: Opposition secures decisive victory in presidential and parliamentary elections
